datasets.name: Public Health Birth Data: Characteristics of Delivery
datasets.description: This dataset is part of a series of seven datasets about Cook County births sourced from the Illinois Department of Public Health and curated by the Cook County Department of Public Health. This dataset includes counts and rates across method of delivery for the County (excluding Chicago). The full data series is as follows: 1) Birth and Fertility 2) Birth Outcomes 3) Characteristics of Delivery 4) Infant Mortality 5) Initiated Breastfeeding 6) Pregnancy Health and Risk Factors 7) Sociodemographic Characteristics of Mother To maintain confidentiality of individual medical records, counts below 5 and rates below 20 are masked with an asterisk (*). Please review metadata and values carefully and exercise caution when aggregating. Some columns only contain data across certain age groups. Some rows overlap across variables and geographic levels and aggregating without filtering may overestimate the counts. For example, aggregating counts across Place without excluding pre-aggregated counts for "Aggregated Region: Suburban Cook County" and "Aggregated Region: CCDPH Jurisdiction" will overstate the counts. Data prior to 2015 can be found here: Suburban Cook County Births (2000-2014)

datasets.description: This dataset includes all asbestos abatement (including Operations and Maintenance Asbestos Removal Permits) and demolition permits received by the Cook County Department of Environment & Sustainability. Under Chapter 30 of the Cook County Code, asbestos abatement permits are required for all asbestos projects. Demolition permits are required if wrecking or removing/disturbing any load-supporting or load-bearing structural member of the building. Commercial, school, and hospital facilities with more than one building must have a separate permit for each building. Data provided is sourced from completed permit applications and may be subject to user error. Please exercise caution and do not consider building-specific information from this dataset to be authoritative. Permit applications that are under review are not included in this dataset.

datasets.name: State's Attorney Felony Cases - Initiation Results by Offense Type and Location Type
datasets.description: The Initiation results data presented here reflects all of the arrests that came through the door of the State's Attorneys Office (SAO). Included in this data set are the defendant counts by city/suburb and initiation, their associated offense type, and year. An initiation is how an arrest turns into a “case” in the courts. Most cases are initiated through a process known as felony review, in which SAO attorneys make a decision whether or not to prosecute. Cases may also be indicted by a grand jury or, in narcotics cases, filed directly by law enforcement (labeled "BOND SET (Narcotics)" in this data). Included in this data set are the defendant counts by initiation and year. This data includes felony cases handled by the Criminal, Narcotics, and Special Prosecution Bureaus. It does not include information about cases processed through the Juvenile Justice and Civil Actions Bureaus.

datasets.name: State's Attorney Felony Cases - Initiation Results by Offense Type and Defendant Age
datasets.description: The Initiation results data presented here reflects all of the arrests that came through the door of the State's Attorneys Office (SAO). Included in this data set are the defendant counts by age and initiation, their associated offense type, and year. An initiation is how an arrest turns into a “case” in the courts. Most cases are initiated through a process known as felony review, in which SAO attorneys make a decision whether or not to prosecute. Cases may also be indicted by a grand jury or, in narcotics cases, filed directly by law enforcement (labeled "BOND SET (Narcotics)" in this data). Included in this data set are the defendant counts by initiation and year. This data includes felony cases handled by the Criminal, Narcotics, and Special Prosecution Bureaus. It does not include information about cases processed through the Juvenile Justice and Civil Actions Bureaus.

datasets.name: Solid Waste Permits
datasets.description: This dataset includes all Recycling Facility and Clean Construction Demolition Debris (CCDD) Fill Operation permits reviewed by the Cook County Department of Environment & Sustainability. Recycling facilities include any building or area in which recyclable material is collected, stored, or processed for the purpose of marketing the material for use in the manufacturing process of new, reused, or reconstituted products. It does not include motor vehicle repair shops which store used parts, drop-off centers or compost operations accumulating less than 25 cubic yards of compostable material at a time, or compost operations where compostable material is used exclusively on site. CCDD fill operations are current or former quarries, mines, or other excavations where clean construction or demolition debris (as defined by Section 3.160(b) of the Illinois Environmental Protection Act) is used as fill material. Data provided is sourced from completed permit applications and may be subject to user error. Please exercise caution and do not consider building-specific information from this dataset to be authoritative. Permit applications that are under review are not included in this dataset.

datasets.name: Temporary Rock Crusher Permits
datasets.description: This dataset includes all Temporary Rock Crusher permits approved by the Cook County Department of Environment & Sustainability. Temporary Rock Crusher permits are required for the reprocessing, storage, transport, and/or final usage of materials generated from construction and/or demolition such as broken concrete, bricks, rock, stone, or paving asphalt. The permits in this dataset are limited to temporary reprocessing activities and don't include equipment registration permits. Data provided is sourced from completed permit applications and may be subject to user error. Please exercise caution. Permit applications that are under review are not included in this dataset.

datasets.name: Transportation & Highways - Professional Services Rankings
datasets.description: The Illinois Department of Transportation (IDOT) requires local public agencies to select and rank (in order of most preferred) three qualified responsive consultants when a project requiring engineering services is proposed. This dataset includes contracts for which the Cook County Department of Transportation and Highways has sought professional services and the top three candidates of the firms that responded. This selection and the ranking of them is performed by the Evaluation Committee comprised of both Department of Transportation and Highways and Office of Chief Procurement Officer team members. Temporal coverage of this data is based on contract award date.
